why: The features still behind Preferences > Experimental, by their row's id there. `scopes` are the commit scopes only about a feature: the notes leave out a commit in one, or whose pull request says `Experimental: <id>` on a line of its own, while its feature is listed here at the release's tag, unless it says `Experimental: none`. `paths` are the code only about it: Verify fails a feat, fix or perf pull request that changes them under another scope until its body says which of the two it is. The pull request that takes a feature out of Experimental is a feat and removes its entry, so the next notes tell the feature as new, with every change to it since the last stable release.
